subject: SCI
title: Science 7 (Integrated)
description: Grade 7 integrated science following the California preferred integrated model: matter is made of atoms that rearrange in chemical reactions, matter cycles and energy flows through organisms and ecosystems, Earth's materials cycle and its surface records a long history, and humans must sustain biodiversity and resources. Every week includes a hands-on investigation with household materials, science notebooks with claim-evidence-reasoning writing, and engineering design challenges.
framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (CA NGSS); 2016 CA Science Framework, Grade 7 Preferred Integrated Model

standards.MS-PS1-1: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.
standards.MS-PS1-2: Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after interaction to determine if a chemical reaction occurred.
standards.MS-PS1-3: Gather and make sense of information to describe that synthetic materials come from natural resources and impact society.
standards.MS-PS1-5: Develop and use a model to describe how the total number of atoms does not change in a chemical reaction and thus mass is conserved.
standards.MS-PS1-6: Undertake a design project to construct, test and modify a device that either releases or absorbs thermal energy by chemical processes.
standards.MS-LS1-6: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms.
standards.MS-LS1-7: Develop a model to describe how food is rearranged through chemical reactions forming new molecules that support growth and/or release energy.
standards.MS-LS2-1: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence for the effects of resource availability on organisms and populations in an ecosystem.
standards.MS-LS2-2: Construct an explanation that predicts patterns of interactions among organisms across multiple ecosystems.
standards.MS-LS2-3: Develop a model to describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.
standards.MS-LS2-4: Construct an argument supported by empirical evidence that changes to physical or biological components of an ecosystem affect populations.
standards.MS-LS2-5: Evaluate competing design solutions for maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem services.
standards.MS-LS4-1: Analyze and interpret data for patterns in the fossil record that document the existence, diversity, extinction and change of life forms.
standards.MS-ESS1-4: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence from rock strata for how the geologic time scale is used to organize Earth's 4.6-billion-year history.
standards.MS-ESS2-1: Develop a model to describe the cycling of Earth's materials and the flow of energy that drives this process.
standards.MS-ESS2-2: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth's surface at varying time and spatial scales.
standards.MS-ESS2-3: Analyze and interpret data on the distribution of fossils and rocks, continental shapes and seafloor structures to provide evidence of past plate motions.
standards.MS-ESS3-1: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how the uneven distributions of Earth's mineral, energy and groundwater resources are the result of past and current geoscience processes.
standards.MS-ESS3-3: Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.
standards.MS-ESS3-4: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth's systems.
standards.MS-ETS1-1: Define the criteria and constraints of a design problem with sufficient precision to ensure a successful solution.
standards.MS-ETS1-2: Evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to determine how well they meet the criteria and constraints.
standards.MS-ETS1-3: Analyze data from tests to determine similarities and differences among several design solutions to identify the best characteristics of each.
standards.MS-ETS1-4: Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool or process.

units.title: Atoms, Molecules and Materials
units.big_idea: All matter, living and nonliving, is made of atoms that combine into molecules and extended structures; people turn natural resources into synthetic materials.

units.title: Chemical Reactions and Conservation of Matter
units.big_idea: In a chemical reaction atoms rearrange into new substances with new properties, mass is conserved, and energy can be released or absorbed.

units.title: Matter and Energy in Organisms
units.big_idea: Plants capture light energy to build sugar from carbon dioxide and water; organisms rearrange food molecules to grow and release energy.

units.title: Ecosystems: Interactions, Matter and Energy
units.big_idea: Resource availability and interactions shape populations; matter cycles and energy flows through ecosystems.

units.title: Earth's Materials and Resources
units.big_idea: Earth's materials cycle through the rock cycle driven by internal heat and the sun, and geologic processes leave resources unevenly distributed.

units.title: Earth's History and Plate Tectonics
units.big_idea: Rock layers, fossils and plate motions record Earth's 4.6-billion-year history at many time and spatial scales.

units.title: Sustaining Biodiversity and Earth's Systems
units.big_idea: Changes to ecosystems affect populations; human population and consumption impact Earth, and engineers design solutions to monitor and reduce those impacts.

weeks.topic: What is everything made of? Particles and atoms
objectives: Use evidence that matter is made of tiny particles
Set up a science notebook and lab safety habits

days.title: Safety & notebook
days.work: Set up a science notebook with a table of contents and sign a home lab safety contract after reviewing goggles, heat and chemical rules.

days.title: Phenomenon: food coloring
days.work: Drop food coloring into hot and cold water, time how long it takes to spread, and sketch a particle model of what is happening.

days.title: Scent in a balloon
days.work: Put vanilla extract inside a balloon, inflate and tie it, then smell the outside and explain using particles.

days.title: Atoms and elements
days.work: Use the PhET 'Build an Atom' simulation to build hydrogen, carbon and oxygen atoms and record protons, neutrons and electrons.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph answering 'Is matter continuous or made of particles?' and take a vocabulary quiz.

weeks.assessment: CER paragraph and particle model sketches.

days.title: Element hunt
days.work: Find 10 elements in household items (aluminum foil, copper wire, carbon pencil lead) and locate them on a periodic table.

days.title: Reading the table
days.work: Identify atomic number, symbol and mass for 15 elements and color-code metals, nonmetals and metalloids.

days.title: Mixtures lab
days.work: Separate a mixture of salt, sand and paper-clip bits using a magnet, filtering and evaporation.

days.title: Compounds vs. mixtures
days.work: Sort 12 substances (water, air, salt, trail mix, sugar) as element, compound or mixture with justification.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on elements, compounds, mixtures and periodic-table reading.

objectives: Contrast molecules with extended structures like salt and diamond

days.title: Chemical formulas
days.work: Interpret formulas H2O, CO2, O2, CH4 and C6H12O6 by counting atoms of each element.

days.title: Gumdrop molecules
days.work: Build gumdrop-and-toothpick models of water, carbon dioxide, methane and ammonia using a color key.

days.title: PhET Build a Molecule
days.work: Use PhET 'Build a Molecule' to assemble 8 molecules and record formulas and names.

days.title: Crystals
days.work: Examine salt and sugar crystals with a magnifier and build a repeating NaCl lattice model to show an extended structure.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw labeled models of three molecules and one extended structure and explain the difference.

objectives: Use density, melting point and solubility to identify substances

days.title: Density
days.work: Measure mass and volume of water, oil and corn syrup and calculate density for each.

days.title: Density column
days.work: Build a density column with corn syrup, water and oil and predict where a grape, cork and coin will settle.

days.title: Solubility
days.work: Test how many teaspoons of salt, sugar and baking soda dissolve in 100 mL of water and graph results.

days.title: Mystery powders
days.work: Identify three unlabeled white powders using solubility, texture and reaction with vinegar or iodine.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a lab report on the mystery-powder investigation with a data table and conclusion.

weeks.assessment: Density calculations and mystery-powder lab report.

objectives: Trace synthetic materials back to natural resources
Evaluate societal impact of a synthetic material

days.title: Natural vs. synthetic
days.work: Sort 15 household items as natural or synthetic and trace three synthetics back to their raw resources.

days.title: Milk plastic
days.work: Make casein plastic from warm milk and vinegar, mold it and let it dry.

days.title: Polymer slime
days.work: Make glue-and-borax slime and compare its properties to the starting materials.

days.title: Research a material
days.work: Research nylon, polyester or plastic bags and write how they are made and how they affect society and the environment.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Take the unit 1 test and present a one-page infographic on a synthetic material.

days.title: Phenomenon: rusty nail
days.work: Compare a new and rusted nail and list differences in properties; start a steel-wool rusting jar to observe all week.

days.title: Signs of reactions
days.work: Run four mini-reactions (baking soda + vinegar, milk + lemon juice, Alka-Seltzer + water, steel wool + vinegar) and record evidence.

days.title: Physical vs. chemical
days.work: Test melting ice, dissolving sugar, burning a candle and toasting bread; classify each with evidence.

days.title: Before and after data
days.work: Analyze a data table of properties before and after interactions to decide if new substances formed.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER on whether rusting is a chemical reaction using the week's steel-wool observations.

objectives: Model reactions as rearrangements of atoms

days.title: Reading equations
days.work: Identify reactants, products, coefficients and subscripts in five chemical equations.

days.title: Modeling with LEGO
days.work: Use colored LEGO bricks to model methane burning (CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O) and count atoms before and after.

days.title: Balancing simulation
days.work: Complete PhET 'Balancing Chemical Equations' intro and game levels 1–2.

days.title: Baking soda and vinegar equation
days.work: Model the baking soda + vinegar reaction and explain where the gas comes from.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: count atoms and balance three simple equations with models.

objectives: Collect evidence that mass is conserved

days.title: Open system
days.work: Mass baking soda and vinegar before and after reacting in an open cup and calculate the apparent mass loss.

days.title: Closed system
days.work: Repeat the reaction in a bottle sealed with a balloon and compare before-and-after masses.

days.title: Explaining results
days.work: Draw particle models explaining why mass seemed to change in the open cup but not the sealed bottle.

days.title: Lavoisier
days.work: Read about Antoine Lavoisier's experiments and summarize how he established conservation of mass.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a full lab report with data, graph and conclusion.

weeks.topic: Energy in reactions: hot and cold
objectives: Classify reactions as exothermic or endothermic

days.title: Measuring change
days.work: Measure temperature change for baking soda + vinegar every 30 seconds and graph it.

days.title: Hot reaction
days.work: Measure temperature change for yeast + hydrogen peroxide and for steel wool + vinegar in a jar.

days.title: Comparing reactions
days.work: Compare graphs and classify each reaction as exothermic or endothermic.

days.title: Hand warmers & cold packs
days.work: Read how commercial hand warmers and instant cold packs work and identify their chemicals.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on exothermic and endothermic reactions with graph interpretation.

weeks.topic: Engineering challenge: design a hand warmer or cold pack
objectives: Test, compare and iterate a design

days.title: Define the problem
days.work: Write criteria (e.g., warms 10 °C for 5 minutes) and constraints (safe, cheap, under 50 g) for a chemical warmer or cooler.

days.title: Prototype 1
days.work: Build and test two designs with different amounts of reactants and record temperature over time.

days.title: Analyze and improve
days.work: Compare test data in a decision matrix and redesign to better meet criteria.

days.title: Prototype 2
days.work: Test the improved design three times and calculate the average temperature change.

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Present the final design with data and take the unit 2 test.

weeks.topic: Photosynthesis: where does a plant's mass come from?
objectives: Gather evidence about inputs and outputs of photosynthesis

days.title: Phenomenon: a growing tree
days.work: Read about van Helmont's willow tree experiment and predict where the tree's mass came from.

days.title: Floating leaf disks
days.work: Use a syringe to infiltrate spinach leaf disks with baking-soda water and count how many float under a lamp every minute.

days.title: Light variable
days.work: Repeat the leaf-disk test at different lamp distances and graph floating rate versus light.

days.title: Photosynthesis equation
days.work: Build a gumdrop model of 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2 and explain how atoms are rearranged.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER answering 'Where does a plant's mass come from?' using leaf-disk evidence.

objectives: Explain how organisms release energy from food
materials: bromothymol blue or red cabbage indicator

days.title: Yeast balloons
days.work: Feed yeast different amounts of sugar in bottles topped with balloons and measure balloon circumference every 10 minutes.

days.title: Breath test
days.work: Blow through a straw into red-cabbage indicator before and after exercise and compare color changes as evidence of CO2.

days.title: Respiration equation
days.work: Compare photosynthesis and respiration equations and draw a diagram of how they are linked.

days.title: Food to body
days.work: Model how digested food molecules are rearranged to build body tissue or release energy.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on respiration and its relationship to photosynthesis.

objectives: Explain food as fuel and building material

days.title: Nutrient tests
days.work: Test foods for starch with iodine and for fat with brown paper and record results.

days.title: Nutrition labels
days.work: Analyze five nutrition labels to compare calories from carbohydrates, fats and proteins.

days.title: Energy in a peanut (demo)
days.work: With an adult, burn a cheese puff under a can of water and calculate the temperature change as evidence of stored energy.

days.title: Growth and repair
days.work: Read about how proteins are broken into amino acids and rebuilt into body proteins and summarize in a flowchart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an explanation of how a sandwich becomes both energy and muscle.

weeks.topic: Matter and energy in organisms: synthesis
objectives: Integrate photosynthesis and respiration in one model
materials: sealed jar with plant and snail (optional)

days.title: Sealed ecosystem
days.work: Analyze data from a sealed jar containing a plant (and optionally a snail) and explain how both survive.

days.title: Carbon atom journey
days.work: Write a story following one carbon atom from the air into a leaf, a rabbit and back into the air.

days.title: Model poster
days.work: Create a poster model linking photosynthesis and respiration with matter and energy arrows.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Review with flashcards and a practice set on unit 3 concepts.

days.title: Unit 3 assessment
days.work: Take the unit 3 test.

weeks.assessment: Carbon story, model poster and unit 3 test.

objectives: Analyze data on resource availability and population size

days.title: Oh Deer! simulation
days.work: Play a tabletop version of 'Oh Deer!' with beans for food, water and shelter over 15 rounds and graph the deer population.

days.title: Population graphs
days.work: Interpret real data on the lynx-hare population cycle and describe the pattern.

days.title: Crowding experiment
days.work: Plant radish seeds at 3 different densities to investigate competition for resources.

days.title: Carrying capacity
days.work: Analyze a graph of a population reaching carrying capacity and identify limiting factors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on limiting factors and population graphs.

days.title: Interaction types
days.work: Sort 20 organism-pair cards into predation, competition, mutualism, commensalism and parasitism.

days.title: Backyard survey
days.work: Observe a yard or park for 30 minutes and record organisms and any interactions seen.

days.title: Across ecosystems
days.work: Compare interactions in a kelp forest, desert and tropical rainforest and identify repeating patterns.

days.title: Sea otters
days.work: Read about California sea otters, urchins and kelp and explain the predator-prey pattern.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an explanation predicting what would happen if a predator were removed from an ecosystem.

objectives: Explain why energy decreases up trophic levels

days.title: Food chains
days.work: Build food chains for a California chaparral ecosystem and label producers, consumers and decomposers.

days.title: Yarn web
days.work: Connect organism cards with yarn into a food web and observe the effect of 'removing' one organism.

days.title: Owl pellet
days.work: Dissect an owl pellet (or virtual pellet) and identify prey bones to build the owl's food web.

days.title: Energy pyramid
days.work: Calculate energy available at each level using the 10% rule and draw an energy pyramid.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on food webs and energy pyramids.

objectives: Model how matter cycles in ecosystems

days.title: Decomposition jars
days.work: Set up decomposition jars with bread, apple and leaves under moist and dry conditions to observe over weeks.

days.title: Mold growth
days.work: Observe moldy bread with a magnifier and draw hyphae and spores.

days.title: Nitrogen and carbon
days.work: Diagram how carbon and nitrogen cycle among plants, animals, decomposers and soil.

days.title: Compost design
days.work: Design a small compost bin and explain how it returns matter to the soil.

days.title: Semester review & check
days.work: Take a cumulative semester 1 checkpoint on units 1–4.

objectives: Build and monitor an ecosystem model

days.title: Build a terrarium
days.work: Build a bottle terrarium with plants, soil, water and small invertebrates and diagram its biotic and abiotic parts.

days.title: Decomposition check
days.work: Record changes in the decomposition jars and explain which conditions sped up decomposition.

days.title: Matter and energy diagram
days.work: Draw arrows showing matter cycling and energy flowing through the terrarium.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Review unit 4 vocabulary and practice data-analysis questions.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Take the unit 4 test; continue terrarium observation weekly.

days.title: Mineral properties
days.work: Test samples for luster, streak and hardness using a fingernail, penny and nail on the Mohs scale.

days.title: Grow crystals
days.work: Grow salt or sugar crystals from a supersaturated solution and connect to how minerals form.

days.title: Rock types
days.work: Classify yard and store-bought rocks into igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic with an ID key.

days.title: Fizz test
days.work: Test rocks with vinegar to identify limestone/calcite and explain the chemical reaction.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on mineral properties and rock types.

weeks.assessment: Rock and mineral ID chart and quiz.

weeks.topic: The rock cycle and energy that drives it
objectives: Identify the energy sources driving it

days.title: Crayon rock cycle
days.work: Shave crayons into sediment, press into 'sedimentary rock', heat-press into 'metamorphic', and melt into 'igneous'.

days.title: Energy sources
days.work: Label a rock cycle diagram with energy from the sun (weathering, erosion) and Earth's interior (melting, metamorphism).

days.title: Weathering lab
days.work: Shake sugar cubes in a jar for different times to model mechanical weathering and graph the results.

days.title: California rocks
days.work: Research California's state rock serpentine and granite of the Sierra Nevada and place each in the rock cycle.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw and explain a complete rock cycle model with at least 8 processes.

weeks.topic: Weathering, erosion and deposition shape the surface

days.title: Stream table
days.work: Build a stream table in a baking pan with sand and observe erosion and delta formation as water flows.

days.title: Changing slope
days.work: Repeat with steeper slope and record differences in erosion and deposition.

days.title: Glaciers
days.work: Drag an ice cube with embedded sand across clay to model glacial erosion and compare to Yosemite Valley.

days.title: Fast vs. slow
days.work: Compare landslides, floods and canyon formation on a timeline from seconds to millions of years.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER on how water shaped a California landform.

objectives: Explain why resources are unevenly distributed

days.title: Gold Rush geology
days.work: Read about how California gold formed in quartz veins and concentrated in streams, then explain the geologic processes.

days.title: Aquifer model
days.work: Build an aquifer in a cup with gravel, sand and clay layers and add colored 'pollution' to see it spread.

days.title: Oil and gas
days.work: Read about how oil formed in California's Central Valley and map where fossil fuels are found.

days.title: Resource map
days.work: Analyze a USGS map of mineral and groundwater resources and explain uneven distribution.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on resource formation and distribution.

objectives: Evaluate how resource extraction affects people and environment

days.title: Cookie mining
days.work: Mine chocolate chips from a cookie with toothpicks, track 'costs' and 'profits', and discuss environmental damage.

days.title: Central Valley groundwater
days.work: Analyze data on Central Valley land subsidence from groundwater pumping and graph the change.

days.title: Resource essay
days.work: Write a short explanation of why one California resource is found where it is.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Review rocks, minerals, rock cycle and resources with a practice set.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Take the unit 5 test.

days.title: Layers in a jar
days.work: Pour sand, soil and gravel into a jar of water and observe how layers settle.

days.title: Play-dough strata
days.work: Build play-dough layers, add a 'fault' and an 'intrusion', and have a family member sequence the events.

days.title: Grand Canyon
days.work: Analyze a Grand Canyon cross-section and order the layers and events from oldest to youngest.

days.title: Index fossils
days.work: Use index fossils to correlate layers between two cliff diagrams.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on relative dating principles.

objectives: Construct a scaled model of geologic time
Explain how time scale is organized by major events
materials: roll of receipt paper or toilet paper

days.title: Toilet-paper timeline
days.work: Build a 46-meter (or 46-square) timeline of Earth's history and mark major events to scale.

days.title: Reflecting on scale
days.work: Calculate what fraction of the timeline includes humans and write a reflection.

days.title: Absolute dating
days.work: Model radioactive half-life with 100 pennies flipped and removed each round, and graph the decay.

days.title: Eras and extinctions
days.work: Read about the five mass extinctions and label them on the timeline.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an explanation of how rock strata and fossils were used to build the geologic time scale.

weeks.topic: Fossils and the history of life
objectives: Analyze patterns in the fossil record
materials: plaster of Paris or salt dough

days.title: Making fossils
days.work: Make mold and cast fossils of shells and leaves in salt dough and plaster.

days.title: Fossil types
days.work: Compare body, trace, mold, cast and amber fossils using Smithsonian Learning Lab images.

days.title: La Brea Tar Pits
days.work: Explore the La Brea Tar Pits fossils and explain what they reveal about Ice Age Los Angeles.

days.title: Fossil record data
days.work: Analyze a chart of first and last appearances of life forms and identify patterns of diversification and extinction.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on fossil formation and the fossil record.

weeks.assessment: Fossil models and data analysis quiz.

objectives: Analyze evidence for past plate motions

days.title: Puzzle continents
days.work: Cut out continents with fossil and rock evidence marked and fit them into Pangaea.

days.title: Wegener's evidence
days.work: Read about Alfred Wegener and list four lines of evidence and why scientists first rejected his idea.

days.title: Seafloor spreading model
days.work: Pull paper strips through a slit in a shoebox to model seafloor spreading and magnetic striping.

days.title: Ocean data
days.work: Analyze maps of seafloor age and ocean depth to identify ridges and trenches.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER on whether continents have moved, using three types of evidence.

objectives: Connect plate motion to California earthquakes and mountains

days.title: Plate boundaries
days.work: Model convergent, divergent and transform boundaries with graham crackers on frosting.

days.title: Earthquake map
days.work: Plot recent earthquakes from the USGS map and identify plate boundaries from the patterns.

days.title: San Andreas Fault
days.work: Study how the Pacific and North American plates slide along the San Andreas and calculate how far LA moves in 1,000 years at 5 cm/yr.

days.title: Mountains and volcanoes
days.work: Explain the formation of the Sierra Nevada and Mount Shasta in terms of plate motions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on plate boundaries and California geology.

weeks.topic: Changes at many scales and unit assessment
objectives: Explain processes at different time and spatial scales

days.title: Scale chart
days.work: Create a chart of Earth processes from fast/small (landslide) to slow/large (mountain building).

days.title: Earthquake-safe design
days.work: Build a structure from toothpicks and marshmallows and test it on a gelatin 'shake table'.

days.title: Story of a landform
days.work: Write the geologic history of a California landform (e.g., Yosemite, Death Valley) across time scales.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Review unit 6 concepts with a practice set.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Take the unit 6 test.

objectives: Argue how changes to ecosystems affect populations

days.title: Phenomenon: wildfire
days.work: Compare before-and-after images of a California wildfire area and predict population changes.

days.title: Succession
days.work: Read about ecological succession after fire and sequence the stages.

days.title: Invasive species
days.work: Analyze data on quagga mussels or Argentine ants in California and graph native species decline.

days.title: Argument
days.work: Write an argument supported by data on how one change affected a population.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on ecosystem disruptions.

days.title: Ecosystem services
days.work: List services ecosystems provide (pollination, water filtering, flood control) and give a California example of each.

days.title: Biodiversity survey
days.work: Survey a 1-square-meter plot in two locations and count species and individuals.

days.title: Biodiversity index
days.work: Calculate a simple biodiversity index for each plot and compare.

days.title: Pollinators
days.work: Read about declining pollinators and explain how that affects food crops.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a report comparing the two plots' biodiversity.

objectives: Argue how they affect Earth systems

days.title: Population growth
days.work: Graph world population from 1800 to today and describe the pattern.

days.title: Ecological footprint
days.work: Use an ecological footprint calculator for the household and compare with world averages.

days.title: Household audit
days.work: Audit household water and electricity use from bills for one month and calculate per-person use.

days.title: Argument
days.work: Write an argument with evidence on how increased consumption affects one Earth system.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on population and consumption impacts.

weeks.topic: Engineering to monitor and reduce human impact
objectives: Design a monitoring or mitigation method

days.title: Problem definition
days.work: Choose a local impact (stormwater runoff, plastic waste, air quality) and write criteria and constraints for a solution.

days.title: Water filter design
days.work: Build a water filter from sand, gravel, charcoal and coffee filters and test it on muddy water.

days.title: Monitoring tool
days.work: Design a method to monitor the impact (e.g., petroleum-jelly air particle cards placed around the house).

days.title: Testing
days.work: Collect data from the filter and monitoring cards and record results.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Summarize results and propose improvements.

days.title: Case study
days.work: Research solutions to protect a California species (e.g., wildlife crossings for mountain lions, fish ladders for salmon).

days.title: Decision matrix
days.work: Rate three competing solutions on cost, effectiveness, community impact and ecosystem services.

days.title: Filter redesign
days.work: Redesign the water filter based on test data and compare versions.

days.title: Stakeholder views
days.work: Role-play a town meeting with a farmer, developer and biologist debating a solution.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a recommendation letter to a city council supporting the best solution with evidence.

days.title: Prepare display
days.work: Create a display board on the human-impact engineering project with problem, design, data and conclusion.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the project to family or a homeschool group and answer questions.

days.title: Terrarium wrap-up
days.work: Make final terrarium observations and write what the year-long model revealed about matter cycling.

days.title: Final review
days.work: Review all seven units with a cumulative practice set.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take the year-end science exam.
